text:
Rina: Quick sync: I reproduced tail spikes on the r5-gpu NUMA rollout. Two competing fixes on the table: slab-splitting (dynamic split of large pages into tiny arenas) vs a fixed-size bitmap fastpath for 4KB subpages. Want to weigh pros/cons before prototyping.

Owen: Paste the short repro pattern?

Rina: microbatch workload with many concurrent 3-6KB tensors, threads pinned to separate NUMA nodes. We see freelist churn and cross-node allocations during bursts.

Kai: Slab-splitting advantage: no bitmap atomics, coalescing still works, and less internal wasted space if we adaptively split. Downside: split/merge code is complex and might have locking on hot pages.

Sam: Bitmap advantage: O(1) tiny alloc find, predictable latency. Downside: atomics on bitmap words and no coalescing -> internal fragmentation. Also snapshotting bitmap for migration adds complexity.

Owen: For both we need NUMA-local preference. If local runs dry, we either steal from remote with a penalty or trigger admission. How strongly do we prefer locality vs avoiding OOM?

Rina: Proposal: prefer local, allow remote steals but add a scoring penalty so remote is last resort. Also expose a tenant-level `locality_score` to limit remote consumption.

Kai: Implementation idea hybrid: use slab-splitting for medium tiny sizes (8-32KB) and bitmap for <8KB. That reduces bitmap metadata while keeping low-latency for the smallest allocs.

Sam: Agree hybrid reduces extremes. Telemetry we need: tiny_alloc_local_hit_ratio, bitmap_word_contention_rate, split_merge_latency, internal_fragmentation_ratio, and remote_steal_count.

Owen: API changes: allocator query to prefer zone: `alloc(size, preferred_zone)` and a status call `alloc_hint_release(cursor)` if we pre-reserve. Keep it minimal.

Rina: Rollout plan: prototype bitmap fastpath (non-coalescing) behind flag on one NUMA class; measure p99 and internal frag. If bitmap wins for smallest sizes, follow with slab-split prototype.

infra-bot: Canary requested -> id=canary-1716007788 target=r5-gpu-numaA cfg={"tiny_hybrid_alloc":false,"bitmap_subpage":4096} 

Kai: Owners? I can prototype slab-split steer, Sam can do telemetry, Owen can wire the alloc API. Rina will coordinate canary.

Rina: Timeline: lightweight bitmap prototype by Fri, slab-split POC in 2 weeks. Keep feature gated. We'll compare p99, CPU overhead, and resident fragmentation after 24h soak.

Sam: Also add a stress unit test that flips alloc/free on many threads to catch ABA/race on atomics.

Owen: Sounds good. I'll open a draft PR for the API surface.

Rina: Thanks all. If the canary shows regressions revert and add more instrumentation.

Kai: :+1:

Sam: :rocket:
